caption:
Four Italian engineers watched their first startup die and started over with $40,000. 

That $40,000 became an $18 billion public offering. Not by building something new. By buying what everyone else had already written off.

Bending Spoons identified stagnated platforms that were once worth hundreds of millions. Evernote. Vimeo. Meetup. They acquired them for pennies on the dollar, sent in a lean team of elite engineers, rebuilt only the core functionality customers actually used, and let the margin expansion compound into the next acquisition.

The margin expansion was not a bonus. It was the strategy.

AI native acquirers are not arriving as vendors pitching a better tool. They are making the acquisitions outright, restructuring the cost base, and reimagining how profit is generated from assets everyone else stopped looking at. That combination of technical leverage and acquisition discipline is producing outsized outcomes traditional builders cannot replicate.

The deal architects always see what others have already stopped looking at.

#BendingSpoons #BusinessAcquisition #PrivateEquity #Entrepreneurship #Leadership
transcript: In 2013, there were four Italian engineers that watched their first startup die, and they were left with exactly $40,000. And that $40,000 just became a $18 billion public offering. And they just simply started out by buying what were one time hundreds of millions and billion dollar companies saw SaaS platforms for pennies on the dollars. Bending Spoons does not build applications from scratch. They buy stagnated, well-known platforms that no one's paying attention to anymore. And we know that SaaS valuations has drastically gone down. Imagine, just think about it, Evernote, Vimeo, Meetup, WeTransfer, AOL, Airtable, these incredible brands, and they're just cash flowing money consistently. They go in and they buy the company and they take an AI-native approach. They have incredible engineers, and they go in and saying what part and what functions of these models are the most important. Let's basically rebuild the core functionality that our customers are using, using AI, rebuild the rest. We don't need most of the team that these companies employed. We're gonna do it internally. So this really lean team of engineers are focusing and rebuilding these entities and running them. Meanwhile, they're drastically increasing the margin and also just enjoying the cash flow. And that's how they were able to leverage their first acquisition into their second, into the third, and eventually going public this year for $18 billion. And this is what I want us to learn from this. There's a clear playbook that's taking place. Doesn't matter whether it's Web 1.0, Web 2.0, or traditional businesses. AI-native founders are identifying how they can leverage the technology to reimagine businesses that are out there, but not just coming in as service providers or a new platform to provide them, are actually using their team and their technology and actually making the acquisitions, which gives them the unfair advantage and restructuring and re-imagining the way margins and profit and growth are generated from the business. This is the new age, and the biggest shift that I see is that VCs and private equity money is starting to open up for these playbooks.
